messages.content: Suppose a sequence of polynomials B_n(x) converge pointwise to f(x) on [0, 1]. Does it follow that the B_n converge uniformly? Ensure that stop words constitute no more than 20% of the total words in your response.

message.content: No, it does not follow. Here is a counterexample: take B_n(x) = (1-x)^n on [0,1]. For every fixed x in [0,1), (1-x)^n tends to 0 as n grows, and at x=1 we have (1-x)^n = 0. So B_n converges pointwise to f(x) = 0. Yet sup_x |B_n(x) - f(x)| = 1 for all n, since B_n(0) = 1. The sup never drops below 1. Hence B_n does not converge uniformly to f.
